content:
anya: Quick RFC follow-up — enrichment sidecar vs central cache. TL;DR: latency isolation (sidecar) vs unified cost/visibility (central). Quick sync?
sasha: read the RFC — main worry is sidecars duplicating KV per pod -> memory & billing explosion for high-traffic tenants.
jamal: @sasha true. But central cache becomes single throughput limiter + noisy neighbor risk. How do we keep billing attribution clean if central caches blur request boundaries?
liam: idea: central cache but shard by tenant key + per-tenant quotas + request tags. Keeps attribution deterministic. Need tight TTLs and eviction policies.
sasha: partitioning helps but increases ops complexity (shard rebalancing, hotspot mitigation). Sidecar isolates warmups to each deploy which is nice for rollout predictability.
anya: we should quantify, e.g. rough GB per 10k concurrent sessions for sidecar. @ops-bot can you surface cache hit stats by service?
ops-bot: ops-bot: query queued: `cache_hit_ratio by service over 7d` — will post results in ~15m :hourglass_flowing_sand: 
jamal: also think about prefix caching semantics: sidecars keep model-specific KV shapes local; central cache needs schema normalization—extra (de)serial costs might offset the network hop.
liam: network hop adds ~0.5–1ms avg; at 1k rps that matters. For strict p99 SLOs central L2 could push us over. Need perf numbers.
sasha: hybrid option: L1 sidecar for hot prefixes + central L2 for cold/multi-tenant reads (L1/L2 cache). Best of both worlds but more complexity (coherence, invalidation).
anya: hybrid interesting. Questions: eviction coordination, coherence (stale KV) and attribution. We should add span tag `enrich.cache_level`.
jamal: add `enrich.cache_level` + `enrich.cache_hit=true|false` to spans. Also `enrich.cache_owner=sidecar|central|hybrid` to map cost. That helps billing/rate-limiting.
liam: also track `enrich.cache_ttl_ms` for diagnosing staleness.
sasha: edge case: rollout drift — new model weights + stale sidecar KV -> inference regressions. Need invalidation hooks on rollout + a fast distributed tombstone.
anya: action items: 1) ops run cost sim for sidecar duplication (jamal), 2) infra prototype central L2 sharded cache + perf test (liam), 3) span schema PR for new attrs (sasha). I'll consolidate into RFC follow-up doc.
jamal: I'll run the sim by EOD tomorrow — quick sim assumptions: avg entry size 1.6KB, 80% hit on hot prefix set.
sasha: :thumbsup: drafting span schema PR, will include OTLP examples and DataDog tag mapping. Example snippet:```json
{
  "attributes": {
    "enrich.cache_level": "sidecar",
    "enrich.cache_hit": true,
    "enrich.cache_owner": "hybrid",
    "billing.key": "acct_123"
  }
}
```
liam: I'll mock central cache perf and provide p95/p99 numbers, and test L1 write-through consistency in hybrid mode.
anya: if no objections we'll convert this into an RFC addendum and schedule a 30m sync on Wed. leaning +1 to hybrid for now.
ops-bot: ops-bot: pinned message added: RFC link + this thread -> https://rfc.internal/redwood/enrich-cache-eval
jamal: one more: cost attribution for bursts — sidecars warm and reduce L2 reads; final attribution should apportion cost to originating request via `billing.key` propagated through cache read path.
sasha: agree — propagate billing key through cache metrics and record cache counters labelled with billing_key for accurate chargeback.
anya: also please emit compact logs on cache misses (fast, small) to help trace cold-starts. Thanks everyone, I'll follow up with doc + calendar invite.
